::: {.bnr-manual-flag .bnr-manual-flag--technical}
Technical Manual
:::

## What this page is for

Use this page to review the evidence used to test the CVD disclosure-control
rules. No routine action is required here.

The review covered **24 consecutive releases**, from January 2024 to December
2025. Each proposed public file was checked against its private source and,
where relevant, the preceding monthly release.

For the current rules, see [Disclosure-control rules](disclosure-control-rules.qmd).

## Validation approach

For each release, the reviewer checked:

- every suppressed row;
- the private pre-suppression value;
- the primary small-count rule;
- the previous month’s equivalent value;
- whether the previous value had been public;
- any release-to-release increment;
- complementary suppression within event-by-sex panels;
- suppression of dependent percentages;
- whether unrelated age and total rows remained available.

The aim was to confirm that protected values could not be recovered from public
totals, comparisons or percentages, while safe values remained available.

## Results

| Year | Releases reviewed | Suppressed rows | Main disclosure situations observed |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| 2024 | 12 | 24 | Primary small cells, quarter starts, temporal differencing, recovery after suppression |
| 2025 | 12 | 8 | Isolated temporal differencing and recovery in the next release |
| **Total** | **24** | **32** | Two complete annual release cycles |

### Key 2024 tests

In January, an event-by-sex count fell within the protected range. The value
was protected in both the annual and Q1 panels. The complete four-cell
event-by-sex panel was then protected to prevent reconstruction from published
totals.

In February, the cumulative count was above the protection threshold. Because
the preceding protected value had not been published, readers could not
calculate the intervening change. The February value could therefore be
released.

In April, an annual cumulative count increased by a protected amount from the
preceding public release, requiring temporal protection. A Q2 event-by-sex
count also fell within the protected range and required primary protection.

| June | 0 | No small counts or increments | Correct |

| September | 0 | No small counts or increments | Correct |
| October | 0 | Q4 began with all event-by-sex counts above 5 | Correct |
| November | 0 | No small counts or increments | Correct |
| December | 0 | Complete annual and Q4 periods with no small cells | Correct |

### Key 2025 test

In March, an annual cumulative count increased by a protected amount from the
preceding public release. This required temporal protection.

The four related annual event-by-sex cells were protected, together with the
four dependent annual sex-distribution percentages.

In April, no suppression was carried forward because the equivalent March values were not public. This confirmed that the process protects small changes without creating an indefinite chain of hidden results.

## Rules covered by the tests

The two-year review covered:

- primary suppression of counts from 1 to 5;
- protection of percentages based on suppressed counts;
- complementary suppression of reconstructable event-by-sex cells;
- differencing between consecutive monthly releases;
- quarter starts and quarter completions;
- completed annual periods;
- release after a previously suppressed month;
- age-specific annual outputs that are unrelated to the protected panel;
- months where no disclosure restriction is required.

## Finding

No erroneous suppressions or missed suppressions were identified in the final 2024 and 2025 test outputs under the agreed BNR policy.

## Limits of this validation

This review covers the observed 2024–2025 release structure. It does not test
every possible future data pattern.

Future review should pay particular attention to:

- negative cumulative changes caused by data corrections;
- more than one independently small cell in the same panel;
- structural changes to the metric dataset;
- new stratifications or new metric families;
- changes to the BNR disclosure threshold or risk policy.

Repeat the validation after a material change to the output structure or rules.

## Technical basis

The BNR rules draw on the *Handbook on Statistical Disclosure Control for
Outputs*, Version 2.0.

BNR protects positive counts from 1 to 5. This differs from the threshold of 10
used in the Handbook’s examples and reflects the agreed BNR policy.

[Open the Handbook on Statistical Disclosure Control for Outputs](https://ukdataservice.ac.uk/app/uploads/sdc-handbook-v2.0.pdf)
